Baytown Roofing Companies and Local Roof Rules

Baytown sits on Galveston Bay and straddles the Harris and Chambers county line, so the rules for a new roof depend on your address. One free call puts you through to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Baytown calls.

Call (832) 662-4107 Baytown permit rules
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Baytown

Baytown roofing companies start with your county

Before comparing Baytown roofing companies, find out which county your roof is in. Few cities around Houston cross a county line the way Baytown does, with neighborhoods in both Harris County and Chambers County. Chambers is a first-tier coastal county under the Texas Department of Insurance windstorm program, Harris County Baytown is not, and that one fact changes the paperwork on a new roof.

The city also has a long memory of wind. It grew out of the oilfield and refinery towns of Goose Creek, Pelly and Baytown, which merged under one name in the late 1940s, on the low ground where Goose Creek and Cedar Bayou empty into the north end of Galveston Bay. Storms off the bay reach its roofs with nothing in the way.

Houston Expert Roofers is a free phone line, not a roofer. When you call, an automated assistant asks about the roof and transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Baytown calls. That company inspects, prices and does the work.

Two counties, two sets of roof paperwork

Harris County side

The older Goose Creek side of the city, the original heart of Baytown, is in Harris County. A re-roof follows the City of Baytown's building rules, and the state windstorm program does not apply. Wind coverage comes from your regular homeowners policy.

Chambers County side

Here the TDI catastrophe-area rules apply. Roof work has to meet the windstorm building code and be inspected while it goes on, and the home receives a WPI-8 certificate of compliance that the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association relies on. City rules still apply inside city limits too.

The quickest check is the appraisal district: the Harris Central Appraisal District and the Chambers County Appraisal District each list only the properties in their own county. If yours turns up in Chambers, write the windstorm inspection and the WPI-8 into the roofing contract as deliverables, with the roofer named as the party that arranges them.

Coastal windstorm rules. In the Texas Department of Insurance's designated catastrophe area (Brazoria, Chambers, Galveston and the other first-tier coastal counties, plus, in Harris County, Morgan's Point and the parts of La Porte, Pasadena, Seabrook and Shoreacres inside city limits and east of State Highway 146), roof work must meet the windstorm building code and be inspected while it is under way. When it passes, TDI issues a certificate of compliance (form WPI-8), which the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association uses to decide whether it can insure the home. Ask the roofer, in writing, who schedules the inspection and when you will get the WPI-8.

When Baytown wants a permit for roof work

Baytown draws its line at the deck, not at the shingles. The city's residential permit guidance puts each part of a roofing job in one of two columns.

Part of the jobCity permit?What to ask the roofer
Replacing roof shingles onlyNot required, per the city's listHow will you confirm the deck is sound before shingling over it?
Installing, replacing or repairing the roof deckRequiredWho applies for the permit if you find bad decking after tear-off?
Roofing with tar pots (hot work)Separate Fire Marshal processHave you applied to the Fire Marshal for this job?
Storm repairs after a declared disasterPermits still required where they apply; fees may be waivedIs a fee waiver in effect right now, and does it cover this job?

Applications, payments and inspection requests go through the city's Citizen Self Service portal, and Building Services answers questions at 281-420-6537. The city notes its list is not complete, so an unusual job is worth a quick call before work starts. A roofing company that works Baytown often should already know the answers.

Bay wind and salt-laden air wear on shingles, fasteners and flashing, and the older half of the city has roofs that have been patched more than once. These are the services most Baytown calls are about.

Baytown's storm record, from Alicia to Beryl

  1. Hurricane Alicia, August 1983. The U.S. Geological Survey says Alicia devastated Brownwood, a bayfront subdivision of roughly 500 homes that had already sunk from groundwater pumping. Residents left Brownwood for good during the 1980s, the Harris Galveston Subsidence District says, and the land became the Baytown Nature Center.
  2. A city that sank. Parts of the Baytown area dropped more than nine feet as groundwater was pumped out, which led the Legislature to create the subsidence district in 1975. The sinking has slowed sharply, but the lost ground means storm surge and heavy rain reach farther than they once did.
  3. The May 16, 2024 derecho. The National Weather Service describes a swath of winds over 100 mph across the Houston metro that afternoon, part of a fast line of storms that tore at roofs and trees across the region.
  4. Hurricane Beryl, July 8, 2024. Beryl knocked out power to more than two million CenterPoint Energy customers. Nine days later, Baytown announced it had waived permit fees for storm damage repairs.

Wind does its damage quietly. A shingle whose adhesive strip let go can settle back flat, so a roof can look fine from the street and still take water in the next sideways rain. If your roof has not had a close look since 2024, the storm damage page lists what to watch for from the ground.

Stay off the roof after a storm. Wet shingles are slick and storm-damaged decking can give way. Keep clear of downed power lines and report them to 911 or to whichever electric utility appears on your bill, since the two sides of the county line are not always served by the same one. Inside, move belongings away from any drip, set out buckets and towels, and keep people out of rooms where the ceiling sags. Photograph damage from the ground and indoors, then call your insurer.

Why Baytown homeowners call the line

The county question gets asked

Tell the assistant you are in Baytown and describe the roof. Once connected, the roofing company can then ask the question that matters most here: Harris or Chambers.

Decking surprises are common

On houses that have been re-roofed before, nobody knows what the deck looks like until the shingles are off. A local roofer knows that soft boards trigger a city permit and should price them per sheet up front.

The bay does not keep office hours

Storms off Galveston Bay arrive at night as often as by day. The assistant answers at any hour, and if the roofer misses the call it passes on your name, number and the problem.

Nothing to pay the line

The call is free. The roofing company sets its own prices and invoices you, or your insurer if that is what you agree. Companies may pay the line a referral fee, and this page says so.

What a Baytown roofing contract should spell out

  • The county your house is in, and whether a windstorm inspection and WPI-8 are part of the job.
  • Tear-off to the deck, with a price per sheet for any decking replaced, and who files the city permit when that happens.
  • The underlayment, drip edge, flashing and ventilation by name, not "as needed."
  • Fasteners and flashing suited to salt air near the bay; ask what the shingle maker requires for coastal installs.
  • A certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the insurer or agent.
  • The workmanship warranty in writing, and who registers the shingle maker's warranty.

If insurance may pay for the roof, the deductible is still yours. Read the roof insurance claims guide before anyone offers to help with a claim.

The deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance says it is illegal for a contractor to offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice saying so. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a property it works on. Treat any offer to "cover the deductible" as a reason to call someone else.

How a Baytown roofing call works

  1. Call the numberAn automated assistant answers (832) 662-4107 at any hour and asks which service you need, since the line also takes heating, cooling, pressure washing and water damage calls.
  2. Describe the roofA leak, missing shingles, hail, a limb on the roof or an old roof you want looked at, plus your part of greater Houston and how urgent it is.
  3. Get put throughYour call is transferred to an independent, locally owned roofing company, which hears a short summary before it picks up.
  4. Deal with the roofer directlyIt inspects, quotes and does the work, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it misses the call, it gets your name, number, city and need to call you back.

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Does Baytown require a permit to replace a roof?

It depends on what is replaced. The City of Baytown's residential permit guidance lists replacing roof shingles alone as work that does not need a building permit, while installing, replacing or repairing the roof deck does. Many re-roofs turn up soft decking once the old shingles come off, so ask the roofer to explain how it handles a permit if decking work appears mid-job. Roofing with tar pots also goes through the Fire Marshal. See roof replacement.

Which Baytown homes need a windstorm certificate for a new roof?

Homes on the Chambers County side of the city. Chambers sits among the first-tier coastal counties that the Texas Department of Insurance places in its designated catastrophe area, so roof work there must meet the windstorm code and be inspected during installation, and the owner receives a WPI-8 certificate of compliance. Baytown homes in Harris County are outside that program, because no part of the city is on TDI's list of designated Harris County communities.

How do I find out which county my Baytown house is in?

Look up the address on the Harris Central Appraisal District and Chambers County Appraisal District websites; only one of them will list your property. Your tax statement also names the county. Settle this before you sign a roofing contract, since it decides whether a windstorm inspection belongs in the scope. The roof insurance claims guide explains how coastal wind coverage works.

Did Baytown waive roof permit fees after Hurricane Beryl?

The city waived permit fees for storm damage repairs after Beryl in July 2024, and it said the permits themselves were still required. It also described an ordinance that waives those fees automatically for 30 days once the mayor signs a local disaster declaration, with City Council able to extend the period. After the next big storm, check the city's announcements before assuming either way.

What happens when I call about roofing in Baytown?

An automated assistant answers at any hour and asks what is going on with the roof and where you are. It then transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Baytown calls, which hears a short summary first. That company inspects, quotes and sends its invoice to you. Calling is free, and companies may pay the line a referral fee. How the line works.
